record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: How does the learning speed and quality of AIξ compare with standard reinforcement-learning algorithms such as TD(λ) and Q-learning, especially in environments where AIXI-style elimination of inconsistent environment programs may behave differently from existing efficient algorithms?

evidence.quote: g) Reinforcement learning. ... For Markov environments (but not for partially observable environments) there are efficient general reinforcement learning algorithms, like T D(λ) and Q learning. One could compare the performance (learning speed and quality) of AIξ to e.g. T D(λ) and Q learning, extending [PH06b].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the universal Bayesian reinforcement-learning agent AIξ defined as follows. Fix a universal prefix Turing machine and let M be the class of all lower semicomputable chronological semimeasures over interaction histories. Let ξ(·) = Σ_{ν∈M} 2^{-K(ν)} ν(·) be the universal mixture, where K(ν) is the prefix Kolmogorov complexity of ν. At each time step k, given history h_{<k} = a_1 o_1 r_1 … a_{k-1} o_{k-1} r_{k-1} (where a_i are actions, o_i observations, r_i ∈ [0,1] rewards), the AIξ agent chooses

  a_k = argmax_{a_k} Σ_{o_k r_k} … max_{a_m} Σ_{o_m r_m} (r_k + … + r_m) · ξ(o_1 r_1 … o_m r_m | a_1 … a_m),

for some horizon m. Now consider classical reinforcement-learning algorithms operating on finite Markov decision processes with state space S, action space A, transition kernel P(s'|s,a) and bounded reward r(s,a):
 (i) Q-learning, with update Q_{t+1}(s_t,a_t) = (1-α_t) Q_t(s_t,a_t) + α_t (r_t + γ max_{a'} Q_t(s_{t+1}, a'));
 (ii) TD(λ), with eligibility-trace update for value-function estimation under a fixed policy.

Provide a quantitative comparison, in terms of either expected total reward up to time T or sample/regret bounds, between AIξ and each of TD(λ) and Q-learning, in finite ergodic Markov environments. Specifically:

(a) Establish nontrivial upper and lower bounds on the regret or learning-time of AIξ as a function of T, |S|, |A|, the mixing time, and the description complexity K(μ) of the true environment μ ∈ M.

(b) Compare these bounds with the corresponding finite-time performance bounds known for Q-learning and TD(λ) in the same environment, and determine whether AIξ asymptotically dominates, is dominated by, or is incomparable to these algorithms in (1) learning speed and (2) asymptotic quality of the learned policy.

(c) Identify environment classes where the AIξ-style elimination of inconsistent environment programs (Bayesian posterior contraction over M) provably yields strictly faster convergence than Q-learning or TD(λ), and environment classes where it does not.
artifact.status_search_result: A search did not find any work providing quantitative finite-time comparisons (learning speed, regret, or sample complexity) of AIξ against TD(λ) or Q-learning in Markov environments. Existing AIξ analyses give asymptotic optimality results rather than comparable rates, and standard Q-learning/TD(λ) sample-complexity bounds have not been juxtaposed with AIξ guarantees. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: AIXI: Universal Optimal Sequential Decision Making (Hutter)
status_evidence.snippet: AIXI provides a theoretical framework for optimal sequential decision-making but no quantitative comparison of learning speed to TD(λ) or Q-learning is provided.
status_evidence.claim: No direct quantitative comparison of AIξ learning speed against TD(λ)/Q-learning is available in standard AIXI references.

status_evidence.title: Q-learning - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Q-learning finds an optimal policy for any finite Markov decision process given infinite exploration; finite-time bounds exist but are not compared to AIξ.
status_evidence.claim: Standard finite-MDP results for Q-learning are not paired with AIξ regret bounds in the literature surveyed.
